title: Offsets instead of pointers
description:
Build a linked list inside a byte buffer using offsets, so it works wherever the buffer is mapped.

```
buffer 256 bytes
push "alpha", "beta", "gamma"
walk: alpha beta gamma
copied the buffer to a new address: walk still works
```
hints: A pointer is only valid in the process (and at the address) that made it; an offset is valid in any mapping of the same memory (lesson 3.02).
Read and write the header and nodes with `std::memcpy` to and from the buffer.
requirements: Nodes are `{ std::uint32_t next; std::uint32_t length; char text[...] }` placed one after another; `next` is an offset from the start (0 means none).
A small header at offset 0 keeps the first node and the next free offset.
Copy the whole buffer to another `std::vector` and show the list still walks.
stretch: Add removal with a free list of offsets.
